newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia detains 22 Sri Lankan illegal immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia detains 22 Sri Lankan illegal immigrants.

text.p: Indonesian police have detained 22 Sri Lankan illegal immigrants trying to travel to Australia from nearby Timor island, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.

Captain Tampubolon, deputy police chief of the West Timor capital Kupang, was quoted as saying the 22 Sri Lankans were detained on Monday evening near the town's Lasiana beach after a report from the public.

Tampubolon said the illegal immigrants had been in Kupang almost a week and a had rented a house from local people in which to sleep and make logistical preparations for their journey to Australia, about 500 km (310 miles) to the south.
He said five local people involved in organising a boat for the Sri Lankans were also detained by police and now face charges of hiding and protecting foreigners without reporting to authorities.
Tampubolon said only 16 of the Sri Lankans had passports and the rest were without documents. He said they had travelled to Kupang by ferry and plane from various parts of Indonesia.
"After they are all questioned, the illegal immigrants will be handed over to immigration authorities for processing," he said.
Antara quoted immigration officials as saying they would be deported to Sri Lanka after being processed.
